items.description: This historic 16th-century fortress overlooks Luanda bay and served as a military center for the Portuguese administration.
An iconic metal structure in central Luanda, often attributed to Gustave Eiffel's workshop.
This 17th-century church is one of the oldest religious sites in Luanda, reflecting baroque architectural styles.
A prominent cathedral serving as the seat of the Lubango diocese in southern Angola.
A monument commemorating the battle that took place during Angola's transition to independence in 1975.
A historic Catholic church known for its distinctive colonial-era religious art and architecture.
A coastal fortification in Cabinda province showcasing Angola's complex colonial defense history.
The primary campus of Angola's largest public university, named after the country's first president.
A modern religious structure serving the expanding community of the Sequele housing development.
A major multipurpose stadium in Benguela, used for significant national and international sporting events.
A modern stadium facility in Lubango, named after the nearby famous Tundavala escarpment.
The legislative building in Luanda where the Angolan National Assembly conducts its parliamentary work.
A small defensive fort providing historical insight into the regional colonial infrastructure.
The main cathedral serving the Catholic population of the Namibe coastal region.
A historic fortress in Luanda with long-standing significance to the city's maritime security.
